title: Boolean values are accepted for numeric-only settings
reasoning: Numeric settings are validated with isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, (int, float)). In Python, bool is a subclass of int, so True and False pass validation for timeout and token-count settings even though they are semantically boolean values, not numeric limits. That can persist invalid configuration such as history_compaction_trigger_tokens=True or llm_timeout=False.
reproduction: Call validate_settings_update({"history_compaction_trigger_tokens": True}) or validate_settings_update({"llm_timeout": False}); the value passes the isinstance check for int.
recommendation: For numeric settings, reject bool explicitly before the isinstance check or add a numeric validator/rule flag that treats bool as invalid for int and float fields.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests verify allowed None, unknown-key behavior, and a valid boolean field, but they do not cover booleans supplied to numeric settings.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting that bool values are rejected for representative int-only and int-or-float settings while real int/float values remain accepted.
minimumFixScope: Tighten numeric validation in validate_field or settings_update_rules and add focused tests for bool-as-int rejection.
